posts.body:
When I was solo, I thought experience meant I had all the answers. I didn't. I was too proud to ask for help and too stubborn to change what wasn't working.

1. Your first five years teach you what works. Your next five teach you what you've been doing wrong. I didn't listen to that second part for way too long.

2. I kept grinding the same way because it was familiar. Familiar feels safe. Safe keeps you stuck.

3. The agents I respect most now are the ones who admit they don't know something and move fast to fix it. Pride costs more than ego.

If you're still doing things the way you did them three years ago, how will the next three years be any different?

You're outgrowing your current situation if you're the smartest person in every conversation.

When you stop learning from the people around you, that's the real sign it's time to move. Not the money. Not the split. It's when you realize you've already mastered what your broker and your team have to teach you. You're ready for agents who push you. You're ready for leadership that demands more from you because they believe you can deliver it. You're ready to be around people who are further ahead than you are.

If you want to talk about what we're building at Lifestyle Design Realty, send me a DM.

I watched an agent this week get a listing at 15 percent above where the market had been. She didn't chase what everyone else was doing. She priced it where the data and the home actually lived. Three offers in five days. Same week, another agent cut price twice on a similar home because he was scared. He was reading the market like it was gospel instead of reading his specific situation. The difference wasn't market knowledge. It was conviction. Sellers feel hesitation. Buyers feel it too. When you show up uncertain, you get uncertain results. When you know your number and why, everything changes. Your seller relaxes. Your buyer takes you seriously. Your offers reflect confidence. The agents who thrive in any market aren't waiting for conditions to be perfect. They're pricing right, having hard conversations with sellers about reality, and moving inventory with purpose?

We hit a milestone last week that stuck with me. Not because of the number. Because of how it happened.

1. Everyone showed up different. Agents who usually work solo started actually talking strategy with each other. That's not forced culture. That's what happens when people believe in what they're building.

2. The deals that closed weren't the biggest ones. They were the ones where someone on the team jumped in to help another agent problem solve. That's the real competitive advantage nobody talks about.

3. When you're part of a team that's winning together, you stop thinking about your next move somewhere else. You start thinking about what's possible here.

This is what growing feels like from the inside. Not everyone gets to experience it.

If you want to talk about what we're building at Lifestyle Design Realty, send me a DM.

I hit a wall last month. Commission was solid but I was burnt out. Same routines. Same problems. No one pushing me to think bigger. I realized I wasn't growing anymore. I was just maintaining.

That's when I knew it was time to move.

If you're telling yourself you're fine where you are but you're not excited about tomorrow, that's a sign. If your broker hasn't invested in your growth in the last year, that's a sign. If you're making decent money but feel invisible, that's a sign.

Outgrowing a place doesn't mean the place is bad. It means you're ready for more.

The question isn't whether you should leave. It's whether you're brave enough to admit you've already left mentally?

I've been on teams where the broker didn't know my name and splits were all that mattered.

Now I lead differently. Our agents know they matter. When a deal gets messy, you've got people in your corner who actually care how it turns out. When you close something good, the whole team feels it. That's not soft stuff. That changes how you show up and what you're willing to push for. Agents stay because they're invested in something bigger than themselves. They work harder. They close more. They recommend other agents to us because they know what it feels like to be led by someone who has their back.

What does your broker know about you beyond your commission number?

We're running with more buyer and lease leads than we can work right now. Mostly new construction in San Antonio and Austin, plus out-of-state relocations. They're warm but they need vetting and nurture. Most aren't ready to move today.

If this sounds like something you'd take on, send me a DM.
